title: Early sine fits at the reported Kapteyn periods raise HARPS velocity error in 2015 to 2018
abstract: We test whether the reported 48.616-day and 121.54-day signals of Kapteyn's star retain their early phase and amplitude. We use public HARPS-RVBank version 02 data. An early fit to 48 nights raises weighted squared error by 93.9% on 104 later nights from 2015 to 2018. Its conditional 30-day block interval is a 52.0% to 149.1% increase. All 3721 tested nearby period pairs also raise this later error, by 36.6% to 95.5%. The 2021 result is less stable: 650 period pairs improve prediction. Central-period controls remain negative in three reductions with time, Earth-velocity, H-alpha, and weight changes. Four best early eccentric orbit fits also raise later error. Known-period signal trials in real residuals recover only 72.5% to 76.5% of coherent 2.25 m/s wave pairs. Thus, the result tests specific early fits and does not exclude all planets. Correlated noise, instrument changes, and early orbit uncertainty remain. No independent instrument confirmation or new planet is reported. The package includes the exact input, source hashes, code, all trials, figures, and offline instructions. Job sci-1107-hp-astronomy-f3356cea6dc7; topic astronomy; machine hp; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Early signals fail the later prediction test in 2015 to 2018. Panels show descriptive spectra, conditional 30-day block intervals, all tested period pairs, and signal trials in real residuals. Gains above zero mean smaller later squared error. The period grid can give positive gains in 2021. These are not planet exclusion limits.

Later SERVAL night velocities at the two central periods. Black curves are the frozen early waves. For display, the other early wave and a fitted group offset are subtracted. Error bars include the fixed 1.5 m/s working term. These panels are not independent fits to each signal.
